newsitem.title: UK: UK links longer Eurotunnel licence to freight - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK links longer Eurotunnel licence to freight - FT.

text.p: Britain will only lengthen the operating concession granted to Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc if the company guarantees to seek to increase long-haul rail freight usage, the Financial Times said on Wednesday.
The paper said Britain's position was put to French officials during meetings on Tuesday.
John Prescott, deputy prime minister, wants the company to work with British and French railways to cut freight on European roads, it added.

Eurotunnel says an extension of up to 100 years is needed to persuade shareholders to accept its multi-billion pound debt restructuring plan and will do all it can to encourage more freight from Britain to use the tunnel, the paper said.
The licence to operate the Folkestone to Calais tunnels is due to end in 2052 but the French government has signalled it would be willing to extend the concession, the FT said.
